items.note: Synthetic-control analysis of 824,634 podcast episodes shows ChatGPT-favored words (delve, meticulous) rose in spontaneous speech, and a preregistered experiment (N = 496) shows a brief chatbot interaction makes participants adopt its words; outcomes are word frequency and lexical adoption, not creativity or output diversity (homogenization is only raised as a concern), so the next stage may want to confirm no diversity measure exists in the full text.

Abstract not reachable (OpenAlex has none, Semantic Scholar 404, Crossref none, SSRN page 403, web search found nothing); the title suggests people generating hypotheses with versus without LLM help, so the full text must confirm the design, N, and whether hypothesis quality or novelty is scored.

PROSPERO-registered meta-analysis of 44 studies (141 effect sizes) comparing human-only with human-AI creative performance, pooled Hedges' g = 0.54 (95% CI 0.27 to 0.81), larger for non-experts and general domains; abstract found via the _v1/_v2 versioned DOI on OpenAlex and the OSF API (v2 posted January 2026).

Firefox add-on ecosystem before and after ChatGPT's release: new add-ons rose 34 percent and drew on broader knowledge domains but were not substantially more novel than existing ones; observational corpus with a novelty outcome.

Participants randomly assigned to write stories with the Story Forge card-based AI tool or a web-based AI story tool (one AI configuration versus another); outcomes include engagement, narrative outcomes, emotions, and creativity, but the abstract does not say whether the stories were rated or only self-reports, and N is not stated.

One survey and two between-subjects experiments in which university students' AI dependence (high versus low) is manipulated and creativity measured, with critical thinking as mediator and thinking orientation as moderator in a 2 x 2 design; the next stage must check whether the manipulation is actual AI assistance, whether creativity is scored on output, and the sample sizes.

Within-subjects user study (N = 16 pre-service speech-language pathologists) of a generative-AI prototype that suggests hotspots for visual scene displays, scoring creation time, quality, and homogenization of communication options; the comparison condition and order randomization are unclear, N is below 50, and the arXiv version is 2507.21811.

Survey of online research participants (34 percent report using LLMs on open-ended questions) plus simulations comparing human-written responses from three pre-ChatGPT studies with LLM-generated responses, which are more homogeneous and positive; no participant receives AI help in a scored task.

Within-subjects study in which 31 designers completed both a traditional and an AI-assisted (psychology-expert AI agent) interdisciplinary design process, with 62 outcomes rated by design and psychology experts for effectiveness, completeness, and applicability; order randomization not stated and N is below 50 (abstract from the PolyU repository page).

PubMed Central and OpenAlex histories of 775,323 scientists show more interdisciplinary and exploratory publishing after 2022, especially for authors with stronger AI-writing signals; the outcome is research-direction breadth and team role division rather than idea novelty, so it is a borderline fit for the observational diversity category and could be out at the next stage.
